cards.explanation: The answer is False. Paul says that if Abraham was justified by works, he would have something to boast about, “…but not before God.” So the boasting goes nowhere with God either way, friends (Romans 4:2). A trophy that nobody in the room will look at is just a shiny paperweight.

The answer is that he believed God, friends. The Scripture Paul quotes says, “Abraham believed God, and it was credited to him as righteousness.” Believing is what the verse names, and that's the whole thing (Romans 4:3). Paul doesn't even need a second sentence for it.

The answer is obligation, friends. Paul says, “Now the wages of the worker are not credited as a gift, but as an obligation.” If you put in the hours, the pay is owed to you (Romans 4:4). That's why nobody throws a surprise party when payday shows up.

The answer is the ungodly, friends. Paul says the one who does not work “…believes in Him who justifies the ungodly…” Read that slowly, because it's a big deal. His faith is credited as righteousness, and it was never wages (Romans 4:5).

The answer is that they are covered, friends. Paul quotes David, king of Israel, who says, “Blessed are they whose lawless acts are forgiven, whose sins are covered” (Romans 4:7). Forgiven and covered, in the same breath. I spent years covered in dust in the back of a junk drawer, but this kind of covered is much better.

The answer is False, friends. David says, “Blessed is the man whose sin the Lord will never count against him” (Romans 4:8). Never counted against him, not now and not later. That's about as far from a grudge as you can get.

The answer is before his circumcision, friends. Paul says it plainly: “It was not after, but before” (Romans 4:10). Abraham's faith was credited while he was still uncircumcised. The order matters, because it shows the credit didn't come from the circumcision.

The answer is believe, friends. Abraham is “…the father of all who believe but are not circumcised…” (Romans 4:11). Since his faith came first, people who haven't been circumcised can still be counted as his children. That's a big family tree, and it grows on believing.

The answer is following the faith Abraham had, friends. Paul says the circumcised are also Abraham's children when they “…walk in the footsteps of the faith that our father Abraham had before he was circumcised” (Romans 4:12). So being circumcised isn't the only thing. They walk in his faith's footsteps, and I love that picture.

The answer is the righteousness that comes by faith, friends. Paul says the promise “…was not given through the law, but through the righteousness that comes by faith” (Romans 4:13). The promise was that Abraham and his offspring would be heir of the world. It came through faith, so there was no paperwork to fill out.

The answer is worthless, friends. Paul says that if law-livers are the heirs, “…faith is useless and the promise is worthless…” (Romans 4:14). He plays out the other side to show it falls apart. If the promise depended on the law, faith would have nothing left to do.

The answer is True, friends. Paul says, “…the law brings wrath.” Then he adds, “And where there is no law, there is no transgression” (Romans 4:15). Those words are heavy, so I'll just leave them there.
The answer is grace, friends. Paul says the promise comes by faith “…so that it may rest on grace…” (Romans 4:16). Grace is what the promise rests on. That's a solid place to stand.

The answer is all of Abraham's offspring, friends. Paul says the promise is “…guaranteed to all Abraham’s offspring…” That includes “…not only to those who are of the law, but also to those who are of the faith of Abraham.” Then he says, “He is the father of us all” (Romans 4:16).

The answer is that He gives life to the dead, friends. Paul calls Him “…the God who gives life to the dead and calls into being what does not yet exist” (Romans 4:17). Think about that for a second. That's the God Abraham believed.

The answer is False, friends. Paul says Abraham “…acknowledged the decrepitness of his body (since he was about a hundred years old) and the lifelessness of Sarah’s womb” (Romans 4:19). Sarah is Abraham's wife (Genesis 17:15). He saw it clearly, and Paul says his faith did not weaken.

The answer is strengthened, friends. Paul says Abraham “…did not waver through disbelief in the promise of God, but was strengthened in his faith and gave glory to God…” (Romans 4:20). His faith got stronger, not smaller. And he gave God the glory, which is a good way to end a sentence.

The answer is that God was able to do what He promised, friends. Paul says Abraham was “…fully persuaded that God was able to do what He had promised” (Romans 4:21). His confidence was in what God was able to do. That's a very sturdy place to put it.

The answer is those who believe in Him who raised Jesus, friends. Paul says the words were written “…for us, to whom righteousness will be credited—for us who believe in Him who raised Jesus our Lord from the dead” (Romans 4:24). That's how Abraham's story reaches us today. The same believing sits at the center.

The answer is our justification, friends. Paul says Jesus “…was delivered over to death for our trespasses and was raised to life for our justification” (Romans 4:25). He was delivered over for our trespasses, and He was raised for our justification. Paul puts both halves in one sentence, and I love that.
